title: Hybrid offset-stable pagination, shard-LRU tiering and overscan probe for dashboard queries
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Symptom: Certain dashboard queries that combine time-window grouping + secondary filters show high tail latency (>2s p95) and frequent stuttering on paginated explorations. Root causes observed: (1) wide scatter in underlying shard offsets causing repeated seeks on next-page requests, (2) cold KV-cache misses for tenant-heavy keys, (3) expensive index validation when multi-column predicates apply.

Proposal: Implement a hybrid offset-stable pagination mode that keeps a compact stable cursor for each page (anchor row id + a light fingerprint) to tolerate intervening writes while still allowing offset-style quick seeks for common short-jump navigations. Complement this with a shard-LRU tiering strategy: per-shard LRU microcache for recent rows + a lightweight global eviction ring to reduce cross-shard cache churn. Add an initial overscan probe on first-page fetch (configurable overscan size) to pre-warm subsequent page fetches for common exploratory patterns. Finally, add a bloom-prefilter stage in the query planner for expensive secondary predicates to avoid full inverted-index scans when possible.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for top-20 heavy dashboard queries reduced by >=25% in staging compared to baseline
Next-page tail (99th) latency reduced by >=40% for paginated explorations in the query set
No correctness regressions: stable cursor tests pass under concurrent inserts/deletes (existing cursor test harness)
Config knobs: overscan_size, hybrid_pagination_enabled, shard_lru_size exposed as server flags and documented
End-to-end telemetry: Grafana panels that break down cache hit/miss, overscan efficacy, and bloom-prefilter false-positive rate
comments: 2026-02-18 - Asha Rao: Created ticket after review of Grafana alerts (dashboard-query-latency-prod) and a small investigation session with analytics team. Attached initial query traces for top offenders.

2026-02-20 - Daniel Kim: Spike implemented a prototype hybrid cursor (anchor id + 8-byte fingerprint) and a micro-benchmark harness. Observed that an 8-byte fingerprint reduces duplicate/skip anomalies in our workload by ~98% on synthetic replays.

2026-02-24 - Daniel Kim: Experimented with overscan_size=50 on three long-tail queries. Warm-up reduced p95 next-page latency by 34% but increased median memory footprint by ~6% for the query workers. Trade-off seems acceptable for exploratory UX routes.

2026-03-01 - Engineering sync: Agreed to implement shard-LRU tiering with per-shard capacity default=1024 rows and a global ring size default=64k keys. Will add metrics for local_evictions and global_eviction_steals.

2026-03-04 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11245 - initial implementation of hybrid pagination cursors + overscan probe. Includes unit tests and a new cursor fuzz harness. Marked as WIP.

2026-03-06 - Perf notes: Local dev perf harness (n=5000 queries replay) shows aggregate tokenized-scan CPU reduced by ~18% when bloom-prefilter applied to high-selectivity predicates. Need to validate false-positive profile on production sample.

2026-03-09 - Design feedback (from PM Sarah Linden): Request adding a console flag to allow customers to opt-out of overscan due to memory-sensitive Dedicated deployments. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-11 - Infra review: Need to surface shard-lru-size as part of Dedicated tenant config; SRE requested a guard that caps global ring growth under memory pressure. Filed follow-up ENG-49902 for operator-side limits.

2026-03-12 - Code review: PR #11245 got inline feedback from reviewer Priya Shah around locking ergonomics for the per-shard LRU (prefer lock-free CAS window). Daniel to address and re-run integration tests.
next_steps: Address PR feedback on per-shard LRU locking and re-run the CI perf suite
Roll out hybrid pagination as a feature flag in staging behind a canary traffic group (10% of console read traffic)
Collect 2-week telemetry snapshot and compute baseline vs. canary for p50/p95/p99 and cache metrics
If metrics look good, schedule a gradual rollout to 50% then 100% and track Dedicated opt-out flags
